title: Character pushout of a split-torus group extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $G$ and $B$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with separated meaning that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $r\geq0$ and $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $i:T\to G$ and $q:G\to B$ be homomorphisms forming an exact sequence $1\to T\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{q}B\to1$ of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site]: $i$ identifies $T$ with the kernel and sections of $B$ lift fppf locally to $G$. Let $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_{m,k}$ be a group-scheme homomorphism. Define $E_\chi$ to be the fppf sheafification of the presheaf quotient of $G\times_k\mathbf G_m$ by the right action $(g,z)\cdot t=(g\,i(t),\chi(t)^{-1}z)$; fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $E_\chi$ is represented by a smooth separated commutative finite-type $k$-group scheme, whose multiplication is induced by $(g,z)(h,w)=(gh,zw)$. The maps $z\mapsto[1,z]$ and $[g,z]\mapsto q(g)$ give an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_m\to E_\chi\to B\to1$. There is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $M_\chi$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and a $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant $B$-isomorphism $M_\chi^\times\simeq E_\chi$, where $M_\chi^\times$ represents frames $\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*M_\chi$ on $B$-schemes $f:U\to B$, scalar multiplication acts on frames, and $z\in\mathbf G_m$ acts on $E_\chi$ by multiplication by $[1,z]$, that is $[g,w]\mapsto[g,zw]$. Under this isomorphism, $g\mapsto[g,1]$ is a frame $\sigma_\chi$ of $q^*M_\chi$ [def-pc-module-pullback] satisfying the equality of frames $\sigma_\chi(g\,i(t))=\chi(t)\sigma_\chi(g)$ on $G\times_kT$.

proof.text: Work on the bounded big fppf site, with a small skeleton and set values in the larger universe. For any $k$-scheme $S$, the group $H=\mathbf G_{m,S}$ is affine and locally of finite presentation: over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}A[x,y]/(xy-1)$. Being affine, $H\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by affine permanence, so it is of finite presentation by the cited definition. It is formally smooth: if $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I$ has $I^2=0$ and $\bar u$ is a unit, lift $\bar u$ and its inverse to $u,v$. Then $uv=1+a$ with $a\in I$, and $u$ has inverse $v(1-a)$. This gives the required lift in every affine first-order thickening over $S$. The definition of smoothness now gives smoothness. These checks use no condition on the field or the base $S$.

Choose an fppf cover $U_a\to B$ and lifts $s_a:U_a\to G$ of its structure maps, using the assumed sheaf exactness. On every $V\to U_a$, each $g\in G(V)$ over the specified point of $B(V)$ has a unique expression $g=s_a i(t)$: indeed $s_a^{-1}g$ lies in the sheaf kernel, which is $T$. The invariant formula $[s_a i(t),z]\mapsto\chi(t)z$ has inverse $z\mapsto[s_a,z]$. Replacing $(g,z)$ by $(g i(u),\chi(u)^{-1}z)$ leaves it unchanged. Sections of the sheafification have local quotient representatives, and equality of such representatives is local, by the cited sections theorem. The formulas therefore give inverse isomorphisms $E_\chi\times_B U_a\simeq h_{\mathbf G_{m,U_a}}$, equivariant for scalar multiplication. Here maps into $B$ and $\mathbf G_m$ are fppf sheaves: an fppf cover is fpqc and the cited representable-descent theorem glues their morphisms. Thus $E_\chi$ is an fppf $\mathbf G_{m,B}$-torsor.

source.place: Tag 049C, remark-fun-with-torsors, question (2); local contracted-product calculation; sites.tex Tags 00WB and 00WK

proof.text: Apply the smooth affine group torsor representability theorem over $S=B$ with $H=\mathbf G_{m,B}$, whose hypotheses were checked in step 1 and whose local torsor trivializations are step 2. It represents $E_\chi$ by $p:E\to B$, affine, smooth and surjective, and represents the scalar action with its torsor isomorphism. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation by the cited smooth criterion. Affineness implies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by affine permanence; hence $p$ is of finite presentation by definition. Since the group is commutative the left scalar action is also a right action, and swapping the two factors in the supplied torsor isomorphism gives $(e,z)\mapsto(e,ez)$ from $E\times_k\mathbf G_m$ to $E\times_BE$.

source.place: Tag 049C, remark-fun-with-torsors; descent.tex Tag 02VL, lemma-descending-property-smooth; affine permanence and definition of finite presentation

proof.text: Apply split-torus torsor frame geometry with $S=B$, $Y=E$, and rank $1$. Step 3 supplies faithful flatness, finite presentation and the specified right-action torsor isomorphism. It gives an invertible module $M_\chi$ and an equivariant $B$-isomorphism $E\simeq M_\chi^\times$; invert this isomorphism for the orientation in the statement. Its frame functor is the one in that cited statement, on arbitrary $B$-schemes. As $B$ is smooth separated and of finite type over $k$, the same theorem says $E=Y_1$ is smooth separated and of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tags 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent, and 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; rank-one frame-geometry specialization

proof.text: The quotient presheaf is a presheaf of abelian groups: the image of $t\mapsto(i(t),\chi(t)^{-1})$ is a subgroup of $G\times\mathbf G_m$. Thus $[g,z][h,w]=[gh,zw]$, inverse $[g^{-1},z^{-1}]$, and unit $[1,1]$ are well-defined. Explicitly, changing the two inputs by $t,u$ changes their product by $tu$, since $G$ is commutative and $\chi(tu)=\chi(t)\chi(u)$. Sheafification preserves finite products and the final object, so these operations and all group identities pass to $E_\chi$. Yoneda represents the natural operations by $k$-morphisms on $E$ and detects their group identities. The maps $j(z)=[1,z]$ and $p([g,z])=q(g)$ are homomorphisms. Over the identity of $B$ take the lift $1\in G(k)$ in step 2: its isomorphism identifies the entire sheaf fibre $p^{-1}(1)$ with $\mathbf G_m$, with inverse $j$. Thus $j$ is injective and identifies the kernel. Every $B$-section lifts fppf locally by $b=q(g)\mapsto[g,1]$, so the asserted sequence is exact. Multiplication by $j(z)$ is exactly the scalar action of steps 2--4.

source.place: Tag 00WJ, lemma-sheafification-exact; explicit quotient group operations and kernel calculation

proof.text: The natural map $a:G\to E$, $g\mapsto[g,1]$, lies over $q$. Under step 4's frame-functor isomorphism, its value on the $B$-scheme $G$ is an isomorphism $\sigma_\chi:\mathcal O_G\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*M_\chi$. On $G\times_kT$ the defining orbit relation gives $[g i(t),1]=[g,\chi(t)]$: apply $t$ to $(g,\chi(t))$. Equivariance of the frame isomorphism makes the right side $\chi(t)\sigma_\chi(g)$. Naturality on this test scheme identifies these as the pullback frames in the statement, using the canonical composition comparisons for module pullback. This proves the required equality, with the positive character rather than its inverse.
